subject: Request: short-term residency variance for debugging EU traces (AtlasHealth)
messages:
From: Emma Li <emma@atlashealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example>
Date: 2028-03-11T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Missing trace data for EU requests - can we hold logs for debugging?

Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing a batch of 502s affecting EU users yesterday (2028-03-10 ~22:30 UTC). Our instrumentation shows the requests reached Redwood but the traceids are missing in the EU shard, which prevents us from replaying and diagnosing the upstream parsing failure.

AtlasHealth retention is on the standard 7-day window; is there any possibility to hold the affected traces for an extra 72 hours so our SREs can triage? This would be scoped to account ATLAS-001 and the following request ids: r-34a7c, r-34a8d, r-34b1f.

I attached a small sample of the error bucket (atlas_error_log_20280310.txt). Please let me know what you need from our side.

Thanks,
Emma Li
CTO, AtlasHealth

---
attachment: atlas_error_log_20280310.txt (text/plain, 12KB)

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example>
To: Emma Li <emma@atlashealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, avery_johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example>
Date: 2028-03-11T09:35:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Missing trace data for EU requests - can we hold logs for debugging?

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the report and the sample log. I can escalate this for a short, auditable exception to the EU retention settings, but we need Security and Legal signoff before we persist any additional data.

Proposed scope: hold only the trace payloads for ATLAS-001 where request_id IN (r-34a7c, r-34a8d, r-34b1f) for +72 hours beyond the 7-day retention. We will:
- Create a timeboxed snapshot in an encrypted bucket (KMS-protected)
- Limit access to a named list of engineers
- Record audit entries and auto-delete at the 72-hour mark

I've opened SUP-9123 (link below) and attached a draft temporary debug waiver for your signature which explicitly authorizes the retention override and defines scope. If you can sign the waiver we can proceed faster.

Next actions for Atlas: please review and sign the waiver (temp-debug-waiver-draft.pdf).

Internal: @Ben @Avery — can you confirm if Security + Legal can approve a 72-hour, account-scoped variance for EU? If so I'll generate the snapshot and notify Atlas of the DocuSign.

-Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

related links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-9123
attachments: temp-debug-waiver-draft.pdf

From: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, avery_johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.example>
Date: 2028-03-11T10:02:00-04:00
Subject: Escalation: request for residency variance (AtlasHealth) — details and proposed controls

Ben/Avery/Markus,

Escalating: AtlasHealth (ATLAS-001) requests a 72-hour retention variance for a small set of traces tied to three request IDs that appear to have been dropped on the EU shard. The customer provided sample logs (attached).

Why we need this: the traces are necessary to reproduce a stateful parsing failure in their pipeline. Without them, the customer will be unable to complete a hotfix and rollout, which risks production user impact.

Proposed controls (minimal):
- Scope: account ATLAS-001 only; selectors: request_id in (r-34a7c,r-34a8d,r-34b1f); time window: 2028-03-10T22:00:00Z to 2028-03-11T02:00:00Z
- Storage: snapshot to eu-temp-debug-<ATLAS-001>-20280311 (S3-compatible, region: eu-west-1), KMS key rw-temp-debug-eu-01
- Access: explicit IAM role (atlas-debug-sre-role) granted to list: jasmine_liu, emma_li (external via short-lived token), and two named SREs (internal)
- Audit: write-only audit entry created and exported to compliance bucket; manual signoff required to release credentials
- Auto-expiry: irreversible deletion job scheduled at snapshot_creation_time+72h

Attached is the redacted policy excerpt and a snapshot playbook I propose we follow. Please advise if any additional constraints are required by Security/Legal. If you approve, I will obtain the signed waiver from Atlas and kick off the snapshot creation.

attachments: redacted-data-retention-excerpt.pdf, snapshot-playbook-v2.md

Thanks,
Jasmine

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example>, avery_johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.example>
Date: 2028-03-11T12:40:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: request for residency variance (AtlasHealth) — details and proposed controls

Folks,

I think the ask is reasonable provided Security + Legal conditions are met. A few practical notes from Sales Ops:
- We should require a customer signature on the waiver before any snapshot is created. No exceptions.
- Keep the scope as narrow as possible (exact request_ids only). No broader account-level retention.
- Prefer generating a one-off, ephemeral export (temp bucket) rather than touching primary storage tiers.

If Security approves, I can own the ticket and monitor deletion. Markus — can Legal review the waiver language (I attached my redline in the ticket)?

Ben
Head of Sales Ops

attachment: snapshot-playbook-v2.md

From: avery_johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.example>
To: jasmine_liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.example>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.example>
Date: 2028-03-11T14:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: request for residency variance (AtlasHealth) — Security conditional approval

Jasmine/Ben/Markus —

Security can approve a timeboxed, account-scoped retention override under the following conditions:
1) The waiver is signed by an Atlas CTO or legal signatory (explicitly naming request_ids and retention window).
2) The snapshot is stored in eu-west-1, KMS key restricted to a temporary IAM role; keys auditable and rotated after deletion.
3) All access must be via short-lived credentials and must be logged to our audit pipeline (we will add a compliance flag: retention_override=72h, scope=ATLAS-001,r-34a7c|r-34a8d|r-34b1f).
4) Security will provision the ephemeral bucket and run the delete cron once the period expires.

If the customer signs the waiver, I approve the 72-hour variance. I will coordinate key creation and the deletion job; Ben, please coordinate the ticket updates to close the loop.

-Avery
Director, Security Engineering

---
Note: required flags for ops: region=eu, retention_override=72h, snapshot_scope=ATLAS-001:requests[r-34a7c,r-34a8d,r-34b1f]

Subject: Re: Missing trace data for EU requests - can we hold logs for debugging? (next steps)

Emma —

Thanks for the quick response earlier. Per Security and Sales Ops, we can hold the traces for a 72-hour debugging window, conditional on a signed waiver from an Atlas signatory. I have attached the waiver draft and a short checklist of steps below. Once signed we will:
1) Provision eu-temp-debug-ATLAS-001 snapshot (KMS-protected)
2) Populate snapshot with the three request ids you identified
3) Grant short-lived access to the two SREs you nominate and to our engineering lead (jasmine_liu)
4) Run an irreversible deletion job at snapshot_creation_time + 72h; we'll post a final deletion log to the compliance bucket and close SUP-9123.

Please review & sign: https://app.redwood.example/docu/waiver-atlas-892 (DocuSign link). If you prefer I can send the waiver to your legal contact.

When you sign, please reply here with the exact SRE user emails who should get access and we will proceed. Expected timeline after signature: ~2 hours to provision and a notification when snapshot is ready.

—Jasmine
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
